prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in League City, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1183; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim reference.
Q: That works. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving east on a two-lane road in League City, heading to the grocery store near the highway.
Q: What happened right before impact?
A: The other car came over the center line. I hit the brakes and turned right, but we still collided nose to nose. It wasn't very fast, maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour.
Q: Did your airbags deploy?
A: No, they didn't. My car just stopped hard, and my seatbelt locked across my chest.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle on your own?
A: Yes, I walked around for a few minutes, but my neck started stiffening almost right away.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic later that afternoon. They took X-rays and said it looked like whiplash.
Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?
A: Yes. I have pain in my neck and upper back, and turning my head to the left is difficult. Headaches show up a few times a day.
Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: I've missed a few shifts. I work on my feet, and sitting or standing for long periods makes it worse.
Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before this accident?
A: I had some stiffness from sleeping wrong now and then, but nothing that stopped me from working or doing my normal activities.
Q: Is there anything else you want to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm following the treatment plan my doctor gave me, and I'm willing to provide my records.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Thank you.
